SMTO-WEB-0036 — SMTO couldn't fully check its research answer

GUID: e8e8cf85-cb4b-5478-acf9-f4c200bd767d
Slug: research-completion-repair-exhausted
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO tried to correct its research answer so every point was backed by a page it read, but the correction didn't work. The answer you got may be incomplete and should say what it couldn't confirm.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the answer SMTO gave and look for a note saying which points it couldn't confirm. This message comes from an older record, so the answer itself is the best guide to what was actually checked.
  2. Treat any point SMTO couldn't confirm as unchecked until you compare it with a source you trust. The failed correction means some statements may not be backed by a page SMTO actually read.
  3. If you need a fully checked answer, send a new message asking SMTO to check again, and name the websites or links it should use. A new request starts the research fresh, and named sources make it easier to back up every point.

What success looks like

  • The new answer lists the sources it used, or clearly says which parts it couldn't confirm.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rely on unconfirmed points for important decisions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A historical web_research diagnostic recorded that the one-shot research completion repair ended without an accepted, proof-validated final answer; current code has no direct emitter for this code.

What this means

  • This compatibility alias describes exhausted completion repair; current exhausted preserves generated work with a partial limitation or derives a bounded fallback from retained observations. This retained catalog alias has no direct current emitting site. The related runtime behavior supplies context only; the alias alone does not establish that the check ran, publication was blocked, or a model call failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect repair_count, original failure and preserved final-response content rather than expecting another correction.

How to fix it

  • Treat this as a legacy receipt code: current runtime.rejected() records research completion rejections and native.recovery.protocol_miss() leaves the run partial at PROTOCOL_MISS_LIMIT instead. Inspect the run's web_research.completion.rejected events and completion_validation; this alias alone does not establish that a repair budget was exhausted, so do not promise another automatic repair.
  • Preserve useful observations and report the original verification failure; do not promise another automatic repair.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The retained response clearly states its actual verification limit.

What not to do

  • Do not claim a current repair budget was exhausted solely from this retained diagnostic.
